" When, in Lanka, thou didst dispatch the great warrior 
Hanuman to seek me out, why didst thou not repudiate me then ? 
As soon as I had received the tidinga that I had been abandoned

sacrificed, nor thine innumerable friends exhausted to no purpose. 
But thou, 0 lion among Men, by giving way to wrath and by 
thus passing premature judgement on a woman, hast acted like 
a worthless man. 
" I have received my name from Janaka, but my birth was from 
the earth and thou hast failed to appreciate fully the nobility of 
my conduct, 0 Thou who are well acquainted with the nature of 
others. Thou hast had no reverence for the joining of our hands 
in my girlhood and mine affectionate nature, all these things hast 
thou cast behind thee ! " 
Having spoken thus to Rama, weeping the while, her voice 
strangled with sobs, Sita addressed the unfortunate Laksbmana, 
who was overwhelmed with grief, saying :-
" Raise a pyre for me, 0 Saumitri, this is the ouly remedy for 
my misery ! These unjust reproaches have destroyed me, I 
cannot go on living ! Publicly renounced by mine husband, who 
is insensible to my virtue, there is ouly one redress for me, to 
undergo the ordeal by fire ! "

brief.summary_1line: Rama harshly questions Sita’s purity after rescuing her, prompting her sorrowful defense and decision to prove her chastity through a trial by fire.

image_candidates.scene_text: Sita, weeping before a silent crowd, asks Lakshmana to build a funeral pyre as Rama stands apart with his head bowed.
Lakshmana reluctantly prepares a blazing pyre while warriors and monkeys watch in stunned silence.
Sita, hands folded in prayer, walks toward the roaring flames after circling Rama.

deep.rich_summary: After Ravana’s defeat, Rama shocks the gathered hosts by rejecting Sita, declaring he fought the war only to restore his honor, not out of attachment to her. He suggests she may go to another protector, implying her time in Ravana’s captivity has tainted her. The accusation devastates Sita. In front of the assembled warriors, she laments the injustice, insisting her heart has always remained faithful and that any contact with Ravana occurred against her will. She reproaches Rama for doubting her despite her proven devotion and the suffering endured to rescue her. Concluding that public shame leaves her no other recourse, she commands Lakshmana to prepare a funeral pyre so she may prove her purity through fire. As Rama stands stern and silent, Lakshmana reluctantly obeys and Sita approaches the flames, invoking the gods before the ordeal.

highlight_spans.why: Rama’s shocking declaration that he no longer wants Sita establishes the central crisis and moral tension of the scene.
The vivid simile of Sita weeping like a creeper torn by an elephant captures the emotional devastation of Rama’s words.
Sita’s defense of her inner fidelity—distinguishing between her captive body and faithful heart—expresses a core ethical theme of purity and intention.
Her command to Lakshmana to build a pyre marks the decisive turning point leading to the famous trial by fire.
The moment Sita approaches the blazing fire before the silent assembly heightens the tragic and sacred drama.

top_scenes.scene_text: Before a vast assembly of warriors, Sita in sorrowful dignity walks toward a blazing funeral pyre while Rama stands stern and silent nearby.
Lakshmana, anguished yet obedient, prepares the funeral pyre as armies of monkeys and allies watch in stunned silence.
Sita with folded hands stands before the roaring flames, invoking the gods as the wind lifts her garments and the battlefield court looks on.
